# sources/object-store/apache-ozone/hadoop-hdds/framework/src/main/resources/webapps/static/nvd3-1.8.5.min.js

## Purpose
This is the vendored, minified NVD3 1.8.5 JavaScript bundle used by the Apache Ozone/Hadoop HDDS web UI to render D3-based SVG charts. It creates the global `nv` namespace, registers reusable chart models under `nv.models`, exposes chart lifecycle helpers, and depends on the colocated D3 3.x runtime. In this source tree its direct functional use is through `static/angular-nvd3-1.0.9.min.js`, which maps Angular `<nvd3>` directives to `nv.models[...]`; Ozone's `static/ozone.js` currently configures a `discreteBarChart` for RPC percentile latency graphs in `static/templates/rpc-metrics.html`.

The checked-in source map shows that this minified file contains upstream modules from `../src/core.js`, `../src/dom.js`, `../src/interactiveLayer.js`, `../src/tooltip.js`, `../src/utils.js`, and many `../src/models/*` chart modules. The minified artifact itself ends by setting `nv.version = "1.8.5"` and referencing `//# sourceMappingURL=nv.d3.min.js.map`.

## Important APIs, Types, And Functions
- Global namespace and lifecycle: `nv`, `nv.version`, `nv.dev`, `nv.dispatch`, `nv.render`, `nv.render.queue`, `nv.addGraph`, `nv.log`, and `nv.deprecated`.
- DOM scheduling helpers: `nv.dom.write` and `nv.dom.read`, which use `fastdom` when present and otherwise execute callbacks directly.
- Shared utilities: `nv.utils.windowSize`, `windowResize`, `getColor`, `defaultColor`, `customTheme`, `calcApproxTextWidth`, `NaNtoZero`, `renderWatch`, `state`, `optionsFunc`, `initOptions`, `inheritOptions`, `inheritOptionsD3`, `initSVG`, `availableWidth`, `availableHeight`, `noData`, and tick/layout helpers.
- Interaction utilities: `nv.interactiveGuideline`, `nv.interactiveBisect`, and `nv.nearestValueIndex` provide pointer tracking, guideline rendering, and nearest-point lookup for charts with interactive tooltips.
- Tooltip model: `nv.models.tooltip()` builds and positions HTML tooltip DOM, formats headers/keys/values, controls show/hide state, and exposes options such as `duration`, `gravity`, `distance`, `contentGenerator`, `headerFormatter`, `valueFormatter`, and `hidden`.
- Chart primitives and composite models: `axis`, `boxPlot`, `boxPlotChart`, `bullet`, `bulletChart`, `candlestickBar`, `cumulativeLineChart`, `discreteBar`, `discreteBarChart`, `distribution`, `focus`, `forceDirectedGraph`, `furiousLegend`, `historicalBar`, `historicalBarChart`, `ohlcBarChart`, `candlestickBarChart`, `legend`, `line`, `lineChart`, `lineWithFocusChart`, `linePlusBarChart`, `multiBar`, `multiBarChart`, `multiBarHorizontal`, `multiBarHorizontalChart`, `multiChart`, `ohlcBar`, `parallelCoordinates`, `parallelCoordinatesChart`, `pie`, `pieChart`, `sankey`, `sankeyChart`, `scatter`, `scatterChart`, `sparkline`, `sparklinePlus`, `stackedArea`, `stackedAreaChart`, `stackedAreaWithFocusChart`, `sunburst`, and `sunburstChart`.
- Model API pattern: each model is a function accepting a D3 selection, stores private configuration in closures, exposes sub-components like `chart.xAxis`, `chart.yAxis`, `chart.legend`, `chart.tooltip`, or `chart.dispatch`, and uses an `_options` descriptor plus `nv.utils.initOptions` to generate chainable getter/setter methods.
- Event contracts: most models dispatch events such as `elementMouseover`, `elementMouseout`, `elementMousemove`, `elementClick`, `elementDblClick`, `stateChange`, `changeState`, and `renderEnd`; chart wrappers wire these events to tooltips, legends, controls, and external callbacks.

## Control Flow
Loading the file immediately initializes the `nv` object, binds it to `window.nv` in browsers and `module.exports` in CommonJS contexts, and installs a `Function.prototype.bind` polyfill if needed. If D3 is not already global in a CommonJS environment, it tries to `require("d3")`; in this Ozone webapp D3 is expected to be loaded by `static/d3-3.5.17.min.js` before NVD3 and the Angular wrapper.

At runtime consumers instantiate a chart with calls such as `nv.models.discreteBarChart()`. The chart is configured through chainable setters, attached to data with D3's `selection.datum(data).call(chart)`, and then performs the standard NVD3 render cycle: initialize/measure the SVG, compute available dimensions from margins, check for missing data, set scales/domains, create or update wrapper groups, bind series/points/bars with D3 data joins, transition changed elements, remove exited elements, and dispatch `renderEnd`.

`nv.addGraph` queues graph generator callbacks and drains them through `nv.render`, allowing chart initialization to be deferred and batched. The Angular integration uses this path after creating `nv.models[options.chart.type]()` from directive options, then installs a resize handler with `nv.utils.windowResize` so `chart.update()` reruns when the browser window changes.

For Ozone's RPC metrics path, `ozone.js` builds `percentileGraphOptions.chart.type = "discreteBarChart"`, defines `x(d) -> d.label`, `y(d) -> d.value`, sets axis labels and value formatting, and passes data shaped as `[{ key: window, values: [{ label, value }, ...] }]` to `<nvd3>`. The directive calls the NVD3 chart model, and the chart renders SVG bars for percentile latency values in `rpc-metrics.html`.

## State And Persistence
This file has no server-side persistence and writes no durable repository or browser storage by itself. Its state is in JavaScript closures, global `window.nv`, the render queue, D3-bound SVG DOM, tooltip `<div>` nodes appended to the document, event listeners, transition state, chart state objects, and per-model caches such as previous scales or highlighted points.

Charts maintain mutable client-side state across updates, including disabled legend series, focus/brush extents, stacked-area style, tooltip visibility and last position, axis scale copies, scatter point caches, sunburst previous arc positions, and resize handlers. `nv.utils.state` captures and applies model state for legends/controls, but this is only in-memory unless an embedding application persists it separately. The Angular wrapper removes SVG and tooltip nodes and clears resize handlers when its element is destroyed.

## Dependencies And Integration Points
- Requires D3 3.x APIs (`d3.scale`, `d3.svg.axis`, `d3.svg.arc`, `d3.layout`, `d3.behavior`, `d3.dispatch`, transitions, selections, bisectors, nests, and formats). It is tightly coupled to the colocated `d3-3.5.17.min.js` and is not compatible with modern D3 module APIs without migration work.
- Paired styling comes from `static/nvd3-1.8.5.min.css`; without it, axes, legends, tooltips, hover states, and chart layout classes still exist but render poorly.
- Integrated into Ozone through `static/angular-nvd3-1.0.9.min.js`, AngularJS 1.8.0, and `static/ozone.js`. The Angular app declares `angular.module('ozone', ['nvd3', 'ngRoute'])` and uses the `<nvd3>` directive in the RPC metrics template.
- Consumes JMX-derived metrics prepared by Ozone controllers, especially `Hadoop:service=*,name=RpcActivityForPort*` data parsed into percentile graph series.
- Browser integration points include global `window`, `document`, `console`, SVG DOM APIs, `getBoundingClientRect`, `getComputedStyle`, `window.addEventListener("resize", ...)`, mouse/touch events, and optional `fastdom`.
- The source map `nvd3-1.8.5.min.js.map` is useful for debugging and research because it preserves module names and original source content, while the deployed runtime is the minified file.

## Risks And Edge Cases
- This is a large, old, minified third-party bundle. Direct local edits are hard to review, easy to regress, and should generally be avoided in favor of replacing the vendored artifact from an upstream build or migrating the UI charting layer.
- NVD3 1.8.5 and D3 3.5.17 are legacy browser libraries. Compatibility risks are highest around modern browser behavior, Content Security Policy, dependency scanning, and any future migration to newer D3 versions.
- The tooltip `contentGenerator` and formatter hooks can inject HTML into tooltip DOM. Current Ozone usage formats numeric JMX values and fixed labels, but any future use with untrusted string data should sanitize or avoid HTML-generating callbacks.
- Rendering is DOM- and transition-heavy. Large JMX datasets, many repeated Angular digest updates, or many charts on one page can create layout thrashing, slow transitions, retained tooltip nodes, or lingering resize listeners if wrappers do not clean up.
- Chart models often mutate input data by adding fields such as disabled flags, series indexes, cached coordinates, or layout positions. Callers should avoid sharing graph data objects where those mutations would surprise other UI state.
- The Ozone RPC chart depends on exact data shape and chart type names. If `angular-nvd3` cannot find `nv.models.discreteBarChart`, if D3/NVD3 load order changes, or if percentile metric names stop matching the regexes in `ozone.js`, the graph area will be blank or fall back to the "enable quantiles" message.
- NVD3's browser-size and axis-label calculations depend on measurable DOM nodes. Hidden tabs, zero-width containers, or delayed Bootstrap layout can produce bad dimensions until a resize/update is triggered.

## Test Signals
- Static smoke signal: load order should define `window.d3`, then `window.nv` with `nv.version === "1.8.5"`, then Angular's `nvd3` module before `angular.module('ozone', ['nvd3', 'ngRoute'])` runs.
- UI smoke signal: navigating to the Ozone RPC metrics route with percentile JMX data should render one SVG per metric/window in `rpc-metrics.html`, with visible bars, x-axis label `Percentage`, y-axis label `Latency (ms)`, and numeric bar values formatted with one decimal.
- Data-shape tests around `rpcMetric.$onChanges` should verify percentile keys such as `FooTime60s99thPercentileLatency` become `graphdata[0].values` entries and `FooTime60sNumOps` populates the sample count.
- Browser interaction tests should cover tooltip show/hide on bar hover, chart redraw on window resize, tab/container visibility changes, and cleanup when the Angular component is destroyed.
- Regression checks for this vendored file should prefer bundle integrity/version checks and end-to-end chart rendering over line-level unit tests, because the minified code is not locally authored and its readable behavior is encoded in the source map.
